chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Making the Chicago records: West End Blues and the studio
summary: They rehearsed in Lil's front room on her new baby grand, Hines and Jelly Roll loved the piano, and titles were often invented in the studio, which had burlap sacks hanging on the walls.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: When you were making those famous records in Chicago, do you have any memories much of those?
Yes I have a lot of memories about them.
Because they, I mean they are very important records you know.
Maybe you ought to say a little about that if there is anything you can........
Yes because I liked the 'West Blues'.

See, we rehearsed that in Lil's front room because she had a brand new baby grand piano and Fatha Hines sure did love that piano. And another thing, old Jelly Roll loved that piano. He sure did love that piano.

Well anyway, a lot of times we wouldn't name down those tunes until we got to the studio. We'd figure out a name for it. Like 'Muggles' and things like that. Oh so many other things. We wouldn't put the name on them until we recorded them at times. They said, well what's the name of this? See, because it was (Firrn?) and Rockwell was handling, and had an engineer, forget his name.
And we would record in those studios with old burlap sacks were hanging down the walls.
